gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the only 2-bay NAS in this field whose maker's own VPN app runs a WireGuard server is the QNAP TS-264 (QVPN Service), at $489.00 on Amazon. That is $99 more than the UGREEN DXP2800 ($389.99), whose pick was priced as low as $296.99. Synology's VPN Server (DS225+) and TerraMaster's TOS VPN Server (F2-425) list no WireGuard.
standout_why: I compared against starryhope.com best-budget-nas (2026-11-02) and both racksandwatts.com pages (homelab guide and DXP2800 vs DS225+). I also checked comparefoundry.com DS225+ vs DXP2800, which ChatGPT got in the second chat. Starryhope already prices the DXP2800 ($389.99, marked down from $439.99), F2-425 ($299.99, sale $254.99), DS225+ (about $360) and DH2300 ($239.99), so prices alone are not new. Starryhope mentions Pi-hole once and says nothing about WireGuard or VPN. Both racksandwatts pages state no prices and never mention Pi-hole, AdGuard, WireGuard, VPN or DNS. Comparefoundry has no prices and no VPN content. None of these pages names the QNAP TS-264, QVPN, or the GL.iNet Flint 2, and none says which NAS OS has a native WireGuard server. Synology's Container Manager page was cited, but it covers Docker, not VPN.
decides: This confirms the DXP2800 as the value pick for DNS plus storage, at $389.99 on Amazon today. It also shows that a native WireGuard server costs an extra $99 (QNAP TS-264 at $489.00), not the DS225+ ($364.29–$421.88 on Amazon), which needs a community package or a container for WireGuard. For a household that only wants DNS and VPN, the Flint 2 router at $169.99 on Amazon or a Raspberry Pi 5 8 GB at $200.00 (Adafruit) costs less than half of any NAS here. That supports ChatGPT's own 'you may not need a NAS' caveat with real prices. ChatGPT's $296.99 DXP2800 card (Walmart) does not match today's $389.99 on Amazon, so the page should show a dated price.
